transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Singh (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (NexaHealth CTO), Priya Kumar (ML Engineer), Sam Ortiz (DevOps), Lina Torres (Product)

Summary: quick check-in on onboarding, access, env readiness and next steps for benchmarks and tuning.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Alex): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll keep this to about 30 minutes, quick updates then action items
00:12 Speaker 2 (Jordan): yeah thanks Alex, appreciate it, we've got a few people here, I'm Jordan, I'll be quick, trying not to take the whole hour
00:20 Speaker 3 (Maya): hi all, Maya from Redwood, I'll pick up the technical blockers after Alex covers the logistics
00:28 Speaker 1 (Alex): sounds good, quick recap: onboarding progress — account created, keys issued, initial models provisioned on our side, customer was going to finish VPC peering this week, any update Sam?
00:45 Speaker 4 (Sam): yeah so we tried the peering, ran into an internal firewall rule, our cloud team has to open 2 ports and the route table, I posted the details in the ticket. we should have it by Friday but not done yet
01:03 Speaker 2 (Jordan): okay that aligns with what I heard. also we need KMS access for our keys — security asked about HSM support and key rotation, any docs on that?
01:15 Speaker 1 (Alex): absolutely, I will send the KMS/HSM integration doc and our SOC2 section, and the network whitelist we use, that should answer rotation questions.
01:26 Speaker 5 (Priya): quick note on dataset, we're preparing an anonymized sample of about 10k records, planning to include a set of 50 prompt/test queries for perf. should be ready tomorrow
01:40 Speaker 3 (Maya): perfect, once we have the sample and the queries we can run the prefix cache + batching profile test, that'll tell us real-world throughput and where to tune KV cache size
01:55 Speaker 4 (Sam): one more on access: can we get temporary log access or a service account with read-only to push logs? makes debugging easier for us 
02:04 Speaker 1 (Alex): yes Sam, we can provision a scoped token and a read-only role; I'll include steps in the email.
02:15 Speaker 6 (Lina): from product side, timeline is tight — we aim to decide on production approach (hosted vs dedicated) by end of month. can you remind us what are the main tradeoffs again?
02:31 Speaker 3 (Maya): sure Lina — high level: hosted is fastest to launch, lowest upfront ops but higher variable cost; dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale plus data isolation; private is for strict compliance or on-prem. Latency vs cost depends on batching, KV cache hit rate, and model variant. we can model costs after benchmark numbers
02:55 Speaker 2 (Jordan): do you have any numbers from similar customers? rough p50 latency for chat at 2k token avg?
03:10 Speaker 3 (Maya): off memory, for a 2k token avg with a mid-sized open model on ded-8xA100-ish infra we saw p50 ~300-450ms when batching is enabled; hosted profiles vary, but we'll give a targeted benchmark after we run your sample. these are noisy numbers but the lab run helps
03:35 Speaker 5 (Priya): great — also question on quantization, we plan to push a quantized 4-bit model to save cost. any incompatibilities?
03:46 Speaker 3 (Maya): we support several quantization profiles; the main thing is accuracy drift. we'll run evals on your sample set to measure quality delta, and we can recommend profiles that balance perf and quality
04:05 Speaker 4 (Sam): we also have strict logging retention requirements — 13 months — is that supported?
04:13 Speaker 1 (Alex): yes, retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private and hosted add-ons exist. I'll include the retention SLA and pricing info in the packet
04:26 Speaker 6 (Lina): when do you want our team to schedule the tuning session?
04:33 Speaker 3 (Maya): target next Wednesday — I can carve 90 minutes to go through batching, KV cache, and running a small hyperparameter sweep for quant profiles
04:40 Speaker 2 (Jordan): ok next Wednesday works for us, tentatively 14:00 UTC
04:47 Speaker 5 (Priya): quick nit — in our internal env we use RBAC via SSO (Okta). What is Redwood's support for SAML/SCIM?
05:00 Speaker 1 (Alex): we do SAML and SCIM for provisioning, can integrate with Okta; I'll attach the SSO integration guide and sample metadata file
05:08 Speaker 5 (Priya): thanks
05:12 Speaker 3 (Maya): on the benchmark side, two runs we'll do: 1) small concurrency sweep to get p50/p95 and 2) 1k request batch test to check throughput and memory usage. if you can give us test queries with distribution that mirrors production that will be best
05:32 Speaker 4 (Sam): got it, we will include a mix of short and long prompts
05:38 Speaker 2 (Jordan): also procurement gave a heads-up about PO timing, likely mid-April if pilot results look good.
05:48 Speaker 1 (Alex): good to know, we'll keep timeline aligned. on pricing — we'll send a pilot price estimate in the follow-up email
05:57 Speaker 6 (Lina): any blockers we haven't covered?
06:02 Speaker 5 (Priya): only the data sample and VPC peering, both are in flight
06:08 Speaker 3 (Maya): ok next steps recap: Alex sends security/network/SSO docs + scoped token steps; Priya uploads sample dataset and queries; Sam confirms peering ETA and grants temporary log read-only; Maya runs the two benchmark runs once sample and peering are in place
06:30 Speaker 1 (Alex): perfect i'll send notes and action items right after the call. does anyone need the recording?
06:36 Speaker 2 (Jordan): yes please, send recording and the shared spreadsheet for benchmarks
06:40 Speaker 1 (Alex): will do. thanks everyone
06:43 Speaker 3 (Maya): thanks
06:45 Meeting end
